title: The shape of a day
hookLine: morning offering, daily word, work, kindness, examen, sleep
tomorrow: what if the whole shape falls apart before noon?

cards: A trellis in a garden is a few slats of crossed wood, nothing much to look at in winter. By late summer it can disappear under the vine. The trellis doesn't make a single grape.
It gives the vine somewhere to climb. These two weeks have been building one, an hour at a time.

teach.b: Here's the frame, end to end. A first thought given to God on waking. The whole day offered, in set words or your own.
Three stops: morning, noon, night. One passage, read slowly. A pause at the table.
Work done heartily. Arrow prayers in the cracks. One kindness, aimed.
At night, the examen, thanks first. Anger settled before the sun goes down. Compline, and sleep as trust.
Some Christians write a pattern like this down and call it a rule of life. Psalm ninety asks for something gentler: “So teach us to number our days, that we may apply our hearts unto wisdom.”
But the shape isn't the fruit.
Jesus says in John: “I am the vine, ye are the branches.” The life comes from the vine.

teach.h: BY GRACE: THE GIFT OF GOD.
teach.b: And Ephesians says where the rest comes from: “For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God.”
Churches explain grace and good works in different ways. Either way, a schedule doesn't earn the gift. A rhythm like this makes room for it, like slats waiting for a vine.

how: Some Christians write a simple rule of life, a few daily anchors of prayer, reading and service, and review it now and then with a friend, a group or a spiritual director.

games.q: what does “the shape of a day” mean?
o: a simple frame of daily habits that makes room for grace
the order of service at a Sunday church gathering
a schedule that proves how holy someone is

games.q: two weeks of the day — tap the pairs.

s: a good rule of life earns God's grace
Ephesians: by grace… it is the gift of God.
in John, Jesus calls himself the vine and his followers the branches
I am the vine, ye are the branches.

games.q: a friend builds a perfect morning-to-night routine and feels like a failure the first time she misses a piece. what does the lesson say?
o: the shape makes room for grace; it doesn't earn it, so one miss isn't failure.
she should add more pieces so the routine is harder to break.
routines don't help; faith should be spontaneous.
games.why: the trellis isn't the fruit. a rhythm makes room for grace; Ephesians calls grace the gift of God.

practice: Find a pen and a scrap of paper and sketch your own day in a few small anchors: something on waking, a word to read, work offered, one kindness, a look back, sleep. Keep it small enough to survive a bad Tuesday.
If you pray, offer the shape itself and ask for the vine.

wordCard.voice: The shape of a day. A simple frame of habits, from waking to sleep, that makes room for grace.

orig.note: the New Testament's Greek word for grace, as in Ephesians 2:8.

carryVoice: Your line: a shape for grace. The trellis holds, and the vine does the growing. Two weeks, shaped.
